Create a calibration objective function from a model, setup table, and data

Source: R/calibrar-main.R
calibration_objFn.Rd

Build an objective function that runs a model, compares its outputs with the observed data prepared by calibration_data(), and returns either a vector of partial objective values or a single aggregated objective value.

Usage

calibration_objFn(model, setup, observed, aggFn = NULL, aggregate = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

model

Function that runs the model for a candidate parameter set. Its first argument must be par. The function must return a named list of simulated outputs whose names match setup$variable for all active calibration rows.

setup

A calibration setup table, usually created with calibration_setup().

observed

Observed data as returned by calibration_data(). This is typically a named list whose elements correspond to setup$variable.

aggFn

Function used to aggregate partial objective values when aggregate = TRUE. The default is an internal weighted sum. The function must accept arguments x (partial objective values) and w (weights).

aggregate

Logical. If FALSE (the default), the returned function produces one objective value per active calibration row. If TRUE, those partial values are combined into a single scalar using aggFn and the weights stored in setup.

...

Additional arguments passed to model each time the returned objective function is evaluated.

Value

A function of par suitable for optimisation.

When evaluated, the returned function:

  1. runs model(par, ...);

  2. extracts the simulated outputs;

  3. compares them with observed according to setup$type;

  4. returns either a named numeric vector of partial objective values or a single aggregated numeric value.

The returned function has class "objFn" and carries metadata attributes used internally by calibrate(), including the number of objective components, their weights, and the names of the active variables.

Details

This is the main bridge between a model-specific simulation function and the optimisation tools in calibrar. The resulting function can be passed directly to calibrate() and related optimisers.

For each row where setup$calibrate is TRUE, the function looks for a variable named setup$variable in both observed and the list returned by model. The comparison itself is delegated to the objective function named in setup$type, using the same convention as objFn().

This means that the structure of the objects returned by model must already be compatible with the corresponding objective function. For example:

  • pointwise criteria such as "norm2", "lnorm2", or "pois" usually expect vectors, matrices, or arrays with shapes matching the observed data;

  • "multinom" expects matrix inputs;

  • penalty terms such as "normp" may ignore observed, but still require the model output to contain the corresponding named element.

If model returns NULL, the generated objective function returns NULL after emitting a diagnostic message.

Aggregated versus vector objectives

With aggregate = FALSE, the returned objective is multi-component: it produces one value per active calibration row. This can be useful for methods that exploit vector-valued objectives.

With aggregate = TRUE, the returned objective is scalar and can be used with optimisers that require a single value. Aggregation is performed with aggFn(x = partial_values, w = setup$weight[setup$calibrate]).

Expected model interface

In typical use, the model function has the form:

function(par, ...) -> named list

where par may be a numeric vector or a list, depending on how the optimisation is configured. The returned list should expose one element per calibration target, with names that match setup$variable exactly.

Workflow

The usual sequence is:

  1. define a model-running function;

  2. read the setup table with calibration_setup();

  3. read observed data with calibration_data();

  4. create the objective function with calibration_objFn();

  5. call calibrate() with the resulting function.

See also

calibration_setup(), calibration_data(), calibrate(), objFn()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
demo = calibrar_demo(model = "PredatorPrey")
setup = calibration_setup(file = demo$setup)
observed = calibration_data(setup = setup, path = demo$path)

run_model = calibrar:::.PredatorPreyModel

obj_vec = calibration_objFn(
  model = run_model,
  setup = setup,
  observed = observed,
  T = demo$T,
  aggregate = FALSE
)

obj_scalar = calibration_objFn(
  model = run_model,
  setup = setup,
  observed = observed,
  T = demo$T,
  aggregate = TRUE
)

obj_vec(demo$guess)
obj_scalar(demo$guess)
} # }
